heading: Binary search on VALUES, not positions
body:
Matrix is row & column sorted but NOT globally sorted—so we can't binary search positions.

**The trick:** Binary search the VALUE RANGE [min, max]. For any mid value, COUNT how many elements are ≤ mid. This count is monotonic, so we can binary search it to find the kth smallest.

heading: Staircase counting from bottom-left
body:
To count elements ≤ target in O(n):

- Start at **bottom-left corner**
- If `matrix[row][col] ≤ target`: all elements above are too (column sorted). Add `row + 1`, move right.
- If `matrix[row][col] > target`: move up

Max n right + n up moves = O(2n)

label: Crux · Python

q: Why do we start the staircase counting from the bottom-left corner instead of top-right?
options: Both corners work equally well; bottom-left is conventional
Bottom-left allows us to count entire columns at once when moving right
Top-right would require tracking visited cells, increasing space complexity
Bottom-left ensures we count elements in sorted order
explain: When matrix[row][col] ≤ target, ALL elements above it (row+1) are also ≤ target due to column sorting, so we add row+1 and move right.
